source_result.name: Step 4: let each fact pick its own depth
source_result.verdict: No: one more right answer than the usual method, and putting every fact at one fixed depth did just as well; not taken forward

entries.question: Would it help to let each fact pick its own layer of the model, instead of spreading every fact over the same five layers?
entries.result: 12 of 72 reworded questions right, against 11 for the usual method in the same run. Putting every fact at one fixed layer also got 12, and a scrambled choice of layers got 10. The new version also moved one nearby-fact check slightly past its allowed limit (86.17 against at least 87.0).
entries.rules_out: This particular way of choosing a layer (one score, one choice of layers, one try, 24 facts) is not taken forward: it did not beat the fixed-layer or scrambled versions, and its gain of 1 is far below the 10 we required in advance.
entries.leaves_open: Whether depth matters at all, whether a different way of choosing layers would work, and whether the choice of layers would come out the same with different background sentences (not measured). One small observation: a single fixed layer matched the usual method while changing the model about two-thirds as much.
entries.next_step: None for this idea now. The ceiling test's repeat run (step 5) is running; steps 6 and 7 wait for its result.
